text:
**MUST READ BEFORE ORDERING**

This visit was BRUTAL! Where do I start. I
placed my order at the kiosk, and when waiting for the order to be made, the counter staff delivered my order to another customer. I approached the counter and asked if that order was mine and I was told to wait because mine was being made so I stepped aside to wait for my order. After waiting a few more minutes, the customer who took my order then brought back the bag with two burger wrappers opened and said his order was incorrect. The staff re-wrapped the burgers and attempted to pass it to me, before I said that I’d like the order to be remade as the previous customer had just touched two of the five items in the order. Reluctantly, the counter staff asked the order to be remade when they passed the opened bag to the assembly line where they took apart the already made burgers, threw out the buns, and reused the inside ingredients. Once assembled, the counter staff passed me two burgers and a wrap, which was three of five items I had ordered. I asked if the assembly line could please remake the order as I just had watched them tear apart the bag that had been passed to another customer and reused the ingredients for my re-made order. The on shift supervisors, Sumeet, said I was being difficult as the burgers were still warm so that meant they were fresh. After sharing my perspective on how the line crew had just thrown out the buns/wrap and reused the inside burger and wrap ingredients to remake the order, they again, reluctantly, remade the burgers/wrap. The order then was passed to me without the drink and fries. I asked the counter staff for the drink and fries, where they poured the drink, passed it to me and said that’s everything. At this point I knew this was intentional neglect. I asked if I could please have my fries, when Summet  approached me and asked what my problem was. I told him how I was still missing my fries, so he personally went and assembled my fries for me. Attached are the photos after I took my first bite of one of the burgers and noticed the fries and drink seemed to be intentionally underserved. Once I fished my meal, I looked for a garbage to dispose of my waste throughout the entire first floor. I approached the counter and asked if they had a garbage when I was told the only garbage can was on the second floor. I asked the counter staff if they had a garbage to dispose of my bag, when the male counter attendant grabbed my bag, threw out the waste, and said “it’s gone, now get out”. I honestly cannot believe the experience I had here. From counter staff, to line cooks to shift supervisors, no one seemed to take any accountability. The drink had not been poured until full, the fries were not full within the medium sized box, with a few random assortment of fries were thrown in, likewise, the chicken wrap had been made without guacamole. To add to the terrible experience, attached is a photo of the bathroom requirements, which mentioned the bathroom is free of charge to McDonalds guests only, as long as you insert 0.50 to use these facilities. Honestly, if I could rate this experience lower than a 1/5 I would. I would not recommend this restaurant to anyone looking for a quick bite.
author: Will

text:
⭐☆☆☆☆ If I could give zero stars, I would.

Only if there were a rating for terrible staff, terrible service, terrible everything. Save yourself the time — this McDonald’s is a masterclass in how not to run a fast-food restaurant.

I wasn’t expecting royal treatment — it’s McDonald’s after all — but you do expect a certain basic standard across the world. Apparently, this branch missed that memo. I ordered a Big Tasty, which is supposed to come with a generous amount of Big Tasty sauce. What I got instead was a dry burger with barely a trace of it.

When I politely pointed it out, the staff member’s response was unbelievably rude. He literally pointed at the sauce smeared inside the box and told me I could dip my burger in it if I wasn’t happy — as if that was an acceptable solution. For anyone with common sense, the sauce belongs inside the burger, not painted on the cardboard like a toddler’s art project.

Instead of simply adding more sauce (a two-second job that costs them a few cents - 0.0000000001c - to be precise), they refused, argued, and I requested a refund. Brilliant business acumen — they’d rather lose a paying customer and a whole meal over a dab of sauce. Even cat food would’ve been a better option, and the pet shop staff nearby would treat you with more courtesy and intelligence than this lot.

To make things worse, my partner ordered a vanilla milkshake and asked for a straw — the staff smugly announced that they “care too much about the environment and animals” to provide one. Yet they’re perfectly fine handing out paper receipts and processed meat. The hypocrisy would be hilarious if it weren’t so pathetic.

Overall, just awful service and arrogant staff, right up to the manager who thought arguing with customers over a missing sauce was a smart move. I’d recommend literally any café or restaurant in Vienna over this McDonald’s. At least elsewhere, you’ll get your food served with some dignity — and maybe even a straw.
author: A. Gbademosi

I absolutely, do not recommend this place.
I already bought a coffee and then had to pay 50 cents just to use the toilet. Nowhere else in the world, in any McDonald’s, have I ever seen such a ridiculous policy. After I used the toilet, they told me I had to buy something again in order to enter without paying. This might be the worst toilet policy I have ever experienced in my life. If you finish your coffee and then need to pee, you have to buy another coffee. If you’re eating and get ketchup on your hands, you need to buy food again just to wash up. Otherwise, you are not allowed to use the toilet. I strongly advise you not to give this disgusting, pathetic business a single cent. On top of that, the staff were the rudest I have ever encountered in my life. Overall, a truly horrible experience, and it’s a shame that such a place exists in the heart of Vienna.

text:
My experience at this McDonald's in Vienna was incredibly disappointing. After waiting patiently for 40 minutes, having already consumed our meal, we were confronted by an employee who claimed we had been in the establishment for an hour, which was completely false. Additionally, we waited for 20 minutes for an ice cream that never arrived.

The treatment we received from the employee was extremely unpleasant. Instead of addressing our concerns professionally, he treated us disrespectfully and rudely, without offering any proper solution.

Furthermore, I witnessed this employee intimidating one of his colleagues, who had been very kind and helpful during our visit.

I hope that the management takes steps to address these issues and improve the customer experience at this establishment.
